newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia to raise minimum wage by 10.07 pct.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia to raise minimum wage by 10.07 pct.

text.p: Indonesia will raise the minimum wage by an average 10.07 percent effective April 1, Manpower Minister Abdul Latief said on Wednesday.
"We will raise the minimum wage from April 1 by an average 10.07 percent," he told reporters after meeting President Suharto.
"Companies (which cannot afford to pay) can submit appeals to government for a postponement of the wage increase. But the Manpower Ministry will check on the companies," he said.
Indonesia in April 1996 raised the minimum wage by an average 10.63 percent.
Latief said he did not expect the increase to affect the inflation rate.
"Nowadays the increase in wages show no indications it affects inflation," he said. We raised the minimum wage as the government is committed to the prosperity of workers.
Latief said Suharto has ordered Coordinating Minister for Production and Distribution, Hartarto, and related ministers to help companies which could not implement the government decision.
"Many companies cannot fulfil the wage increase because of bad management. The government will help them," Latief said, without giving details.
Indonesians working in the capital Jakarta will get the most from the pay hike, with their minimum monthly wage increasing to 172,500 rupiah from 156,000.
